rows.label: Concept
rows.text: An ecosystem (Tansley, 1935) is nature's self-sustaining unit: a biotic community running on its abiotic environment through one-way energy flow and cyclic nutrients. Its structure has three layers — abiotic components (inorganic nutrients, organic detritus, climate), biotic components (producers, consumers, decomposers) and functional links (energy flow, nutrient cycling, homeostasis).…

Net primary productivity = gross primary productivity − respiration of the producers.

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Littoral vs limnetic:** littoral = shallow near-shore zone with rooted plants; limnetic = open, well-lit water of plankton and fish.  ·  **Ecosystem vs community:** community = only the living populations; ecosystem = community + abiotic environment + their interactions.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Name a Nepali forest type if you can, then still give the universal strata. The strata are what the mark scheme wants.  ·  Trophic level and zone are different. Limnetic is a place. Producer is a feeding role.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***Pond*** — the classic diagram ecosystem: phytoplankton → zooplankton → fish with benthic decomposers.  ·  ***Forest*** — high-biomass ecosystem where the detritus chain outweighs the grazing chain.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: The ecosystem-structure question is the highest-marked repeated question (5m, 2023 + 2024) — memorise the three-component skeleton and practise the pond diagram.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Compare pond and forest in two columns: producers, consumers, decomposers, main abiotic medium.  ·  Calculate the energy at each trophic level from a given producer input.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: "I-O-C / P-C-D: Inorganic, Organic, Climate / Producers, Consumers, Decomposers."

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **Short answer (2m):** Name the zones of a pond ecosystem. **Answer.** **Littoral** — shallow edges, rooted plants, snails, insect larvae, frogs. **Limnetic** — open water down to light depth, phytoplankton, zooplankton, fish. **Profundal/benthic** — deep, dark bottom, decomposers and anaerobic bacteria.

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: Most-tested: definition + structure + diagram (2023, 2024). Diagram-worthy: pond cross-section with zones, arrows for energy and nutrients.

rows.text: 2.2 The pond ecosystem (standard diagram example) · Zone | Depth | Inhabitants · **Littoral** | Shallow edges | Rooted plants, snails, insect larvae, frogs · **Limnetic** | Open water to light depth | Phytoplankton (algae), zooplankton, fish · **Profundal/benthic** | Below light penetration | Decomposers, bottom dwellers, anaerobic bacteria  ·  2.3 The forest ecosystem · Layer | Inhabitants · **Canopy (upper)** | Birds, monkeys, epiphytes, lianas · **Understorey** | Shade-tolerant shrubs, small mammals, insects · **Forest floor** | Leaf litter, earthworms, fungi, bacteria — the detritus engine

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **Self-sustaining test:** a real ecosystem needs only sunlight — everything else (matter) is internally recycled; artificial ecosystems (aquarium) need constant human input.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Ecosystem (Tansley, 1935): self-sustaining unit = biotic community + abiotic environment + energy flow + nutrient cycling.  ·  Structure: abiotic (inorganic, organic, climate) + biotic (producers, consumers, decomposers) + functional (energy flow, cycling, homeostasis).  ·  Pond zones: littoral, limnetic, profundal/benthic. Forest layers: canopy, understorey, floor (detritus chain dominates).  ·  5m PYQ repeated 2023 and 2024 — definition + structure + diagram.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Ecosystems need no matter imports — a sealed terrarium with light can run for years on recycled water, CO₂ and nutrients.

rows.label: MCQ drill
rows.text: The profundal zone of a pond is → B  ·  Under the ten percent law, 10,000 kJ in producers leaves about how much at the tertiary consumer? → D
